items.stem: You want to tell a robot how to get a cookie from a jar. Why must your steps be in the right order?

options.text: Because the robot does each step exactly as told, one after another
options.rationale: Correct: a computer follows steps in order and cannot guess what you meant.
The robot has no feelings; order matters because steps run one after another.

options.text: Because order never matters to robots
options.rationale: Order does matter; wrong order gives the wrong result.
The shape of the cookie does not change how steps run.

items.explanation: Correct: a computer follows steps in order and cannot guess what you meant.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO of these are examples of a loop (something that repeats)? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: doing the same hop again and again is a repeat/loop.

options.text: Clap your hands every time the music plays
options.rationale: Correct: repeating the clap each time is a loop.
Doing something a single time is not a repeat.
Saying it once is a single step, not a loop.

items.explanation: Correct: doing the same hop again and again is a repeat/loop.

items.stem: A plan says: 1) put on socks 2) put on shoes 3) put on socks. There is a bug. What should you do?

options.text: Remove or fix the repeated 'put on socks' step so the plan works
options.rationale: Correct: debugging means finding the wrong step and fixing it.

options.text: Throw the plan away and never try again
options.rationale: We fix bugs; we do not give up.
Adding steps does not fix the wrong one.

options.text: Tell the shoes to try harder
options.rationale: Shoes cannot follow instructions; we fix the plan.

items.explanation: Correct: debugging means finding the wrong step and fixing it.
